stories.title: Alibaba plans $10 billion Hong Kong share placement to fund AI spending
stories.simple_summary: Alibaba, a large Chinese company, is raising $10 billion to spend on developing AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people who own Alibaba stock — it doesn't directly change anything for your daily life or small business.

stories.title: A free AI model is winning over developers. And nobody knows whose servers it runs on
stories.simple_summary: A free AI tool that many computer programmers like is becoming very popular, but nobody is certain who is paying to run it or where the computers are located.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use free AI tools, this is a reminder to be cautious about where your information goes — but this story is mainly for tech professionals.

stories.title: Harvard’s $699 startup bootcamp offers AI avatars of its instructors
stories.simple_summary: Harvard Business School created AI versions of its teachers that give feedback to students practicing their business pitches, like having a coach available 24/7.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to people taking Harvard's expensive bootcamp — it doesn't affect most small business owners unless you're interested in using AI coaching tools yourself.

stories.title: Anthropic Is Reportedly Being Upfront With Would-Be Investors About AI Backlash
stories.simple_summary: A company called Anthropic that makes AI is being honest with people who might invest money in them about concerns people have regarding AI safety.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI ‘teammate’ just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research
stories.simple_summary: A new AI company created by former Google researchers claims their AI can read and replicate scientific research papers better than systems made by OpenAI and Anthropic.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters mainly to researchers and investors — for small business owners, just know that different AI tools are competing to be better at different tasks.

stories.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, now wants California to make its new AI safety rules stricter than currently planned, even though they opposed similar rules before.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about government regulation and doesn't directly affect you right now, though it could shape how AI tools work in the future.

stories.title: Frontier AI labs still won’t say how they’d contain a rogue model
stories.simple_summary: A study found that major AI companies don't have clear public plans for what to do if their AI systems go wrong or act dangerously.
stories.why_it_matters: This raises legitimate safety concerns — it suggests AI companies should have better safeguards, though for ordinary people this is still a future worry rather than an immediate problem.

stories.title: AI decodes DNA initiator sequence found in about 60% of human genes
stories.simple_summary: AI has helped scientists understand a pattern in human DNA that appears in about 60% of our genes.
stories.why_it_matters: This could help medical researchers develop better treatments in the future, but this is a long-term scientific advance, not something affecting you today.

stories.title: Billionaire David Tepper Sold His Fund's Sandisk Stake in Favor of This Trillion-Dollar Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock
stories.simple_summary: A wealthy investor sold his company's SanDisk computer chip stock to invest in AI-related companies instead, betting that AI is a better opportunity.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people who own those stocks — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Would even an AI disaster on the scale of Hiroshima be enough to make humankind protect itself? I fear not
stories.simple_summary: An opinion piece argues that even if AI caused a disaster as big as Hiroshima, people might still not do enough to protect themselves from future AI risks.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a scary opinion piece about the distant future — it doesn't require action from you today.

stories.title: The Results of Middle and High School Students Using AI Are Extremely Ominous
stories.simple_summary: Research suggests that middle and high school students using AI tools are showing concerning results, though the article doesn't explain specifically what those concerns are.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have school-age children or grandchildren, this suggests it's worth thinking about how they use AI — but you'd need more information to know what specific problems to watch for.

stories.title: Alphabet and Amazon Are Investing $420 Billion in Artificial Intelligence (AI) Infrastructure: 4 Hardware Stocks Set to Profit
stories.simple_summary: Google and Amazon are planning to spend a combined $420 billion building computer servers and equipment for AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors in computer hardware companies — it shows AI is becoming a huge priority for big companies, but doesn't directly change your daily life.
